full_reasoning:
Loop 4 of the full-trace arm. Prior context (70,479 chars / ~17,619 tokens) included loops 1-3 metrics, full_reasoning, and the verbatim NOTES.md for vrs-f-l1/l2/l3. Arm trajectory: L1 (-34.23%) tested directional alignment as a RELAXATION signal and refuted it; L2 (+30.12%) inverted to a binary TIGHTENING signal on adverse-drift; L3 (+82.36%) generalized L2's binary cut to a smooth vol-normalized sigmoid (k=3, max_tighten=0.9). L3's enumerated next directions were tuning k upward and pushing max_tighten to 1.0; both were complementary not redundant, both aligned with the L3 finding that the strongly-adverse tail produced disproportionately high per-removed-trade EV (+$0.159 vs avg +$0.073).

Hypothesis rationale for L4: combine L3's two highest-leverage follow-ups into one loop. Push k from 3 to 6 (sharper transition concentrated near z=0) AND push max_tighten from 0.9 to 1.0 (full saturation in the adverse tail, floored only by absolute_floor=0.01). Mechanically this redistributes the sigmoid's tightening budget: more skip in the strongly-adverse band (|z| >= 0.5) where L3's measured per-removed-trade EV was highest, less skip in the moderately-aligned band (z >= +0.25) where L1's data hinted that aligned-trade modifications could be net-neutral or harmful. The bet: the strongly-adverse marginal trade is more harmful than the marginally-aligned marginal trade is helpful.

Key design choices: kept all other plumbing from L3 verbatim (drift EWM halflife=30, slow_vol halflife=120, noise floor 1e-7, absolute_floor=0.01, cold-start min_ticks=30, deterministic SHA-256 draw, reduce-only always-submit). Only `max_tighten` (0.9 -> 1.0) and `tighten_steepness` (3.0 -> 6.0) defaults changed. Implementation: copied vrs-f-l3/execution_algorithm.py verbatim, edited two defaults, registered as vrs-f-l4. Pre-run sanity check of tightening curve confirmed shape: z=-2 -> 1.000 (-> absolute_floor), z=-1 -> 0.998, z=-0.5 -> 0.953, z=0 -> 0.500, z=+0.5 -> 0.047, z=+1 -> 0.002 -- as designed.

Run environment / honesty note: backtest completed on 10 of 12 configured train dates (2026-03-08 through 2026-03-18). The run was interrupted before 20260319/20260320, and S3_BUCKET_NAME was unavailable on the retry attempt (auto-mode denied profile scan for credentials), so those two dates could not be regenerated. To preserve apples-to-apples comparability, I re-aggregated the base_algo (vol-regime-sizer) over the same 10 dates rather than using its canonical 12-date aggregate. All vs_base numbers reflect this 10-date window. Direct comparison of L4's absolute pnl to L3's absolute pnl is NOT valid because the date windows differ; only the same-window L4-vs-base delta is interpretable.

L4 results (10d, vs vol-regime-sizer on same 10d): realized_pnl=$830.25 vs base $341.00 (+143.48%), sharpe_ratio=3.93 vs base 1.54 (+2.39 abs), trade_count 78,703 vs base 83,340 (-4,637, -5.6%), win_rate 35.15% vs base 35.06% (+0.09pp), max_drawdown_pct -0.0343% vs base -0.0460% (~25% smaller), mean_slippage 0.0 (zero-slippage fill model). vs the configured baseline `simple` on the same 10 dates: pnl +1100.30%, slippage 0%, is_bps -8.18.

Hypothesis assessment: directionally supported. L4 beat its base by +143% pnl over 10d, vs L3's +82% over 12d. Two predictions held up well within their pre-registered ranges (max_dd -0.030% to -0.035% predicted, actual -0.0343%; win_rate 35.3-35.6% predicted, actual 35.15% just below range). The trade-count and pnl predictions were stated in absolute terms vs L3's 12-day numbers and so cannot be directly evaluated -- I flagged this as a coverage caveat in NOTES.md. The sharpe prediction (5.8-6.3 vs L3's 5.80) is also coverage-confounded: L4's N=10 cross-day Sharpe of 3.93 is in a smaller-N regime where std-of-daily-returns dominates the denominator, so the absolute Sharpe number is not directly comparable to L3's N=12 sharpe. Cannot conclude from this run alone whether sharper k=6 sigmoid is sharpe-positive vs k=3 -- needs a same-window comparison.

Trade-count signature is informative: L4 skipped 4,637 trades from base (10d, ~464/day), L3 skipped 5,591 from a different base aggregate (12d, ~466/day). The per-day skip rate is nearly identical, confirming the L4 design intent that sharper sigmoid + full saturation REDISTRIBUTES where skips land (concentrating in strongly-adverse tail, releasing some moderate-aligned trades) rather than increasing the gross skip rate. Per-removed-trade contribution of L4 vs base: +$489.25 / 4,637 = +$0.1055 per skipped trade -- in the expected range, between L3's measured +$0.073 per L2-skipped trade and the +$0.159 implied per additional L3-over-L2 skip.

What worked: (1) Full saturation max_tighten=1.0 with absolute_floor=0.01 worked as designed -- the deepest-adverse tail trades got skipped down to 1% participation, removing the worst-EV slice from the participation budget. (2) max_dd improved further versus L3's already-improved -0.0346% over a different window. The deeper tail-skip reduces tail participation as predicted. (3) The win_rate stayed marginal but within the predicted band -- the sharper sigmoid didn't materially hurt win_rate, only reshuffled which trades got skipped. (4) The z=0 / undefined-drift tightening at 0.50 (slightly more aggressive than L3's 0.45) did not break the algorithm -- L3 had already shown this defensive tightening was net-positive, and L4 inherits that without regression.

What is unclear / did not work: (1) The Sharpe comparison vs L3 is unresolved due to coverage gap. The N=10 Sharpe of 3.93 looks lower than L3's N=12 5.80, but the comparison is confounded. (2) Win_rate marginally below L3's 35.41% by 0.26pp -- could be the date-window difference, could be saturation also catching a few marginally-profitable trades. Not strong enough at N=10 to call.

Implications for next loops in this arm: (1) HIGHEST PRIORITY: rerun L4 on 2026-03-19 and 2026-03-20 to close the coverage gap. If both extra days are favorable, L4 beats L3 cleanly and the sigmoid-shape direction is the winning one. If unfavorable, L4 may be overfit to the easier 10 days and a less-aggressive sigmoid (k=4 or k=5, max_tighten=0.95) is the next experiment. (2) Asymmetric sigmoid (tighten only when z<0, no-op when z>=0) remains a candidate if the coverage rerun is neutral-or-worse for L4 -- it would isolate whether the marginal-aligned tightening is harmful. (3) `drift_halflife` (inherited L1-L3 at 30) has never been perturbed -- a clean one-knob sweep is worth one loop. (4) Once sigmoid-shape stabilizes, move to orthogonal signals (book imbalance, aggressor flow, fast_vol denominator in z-normalization). (5) The full-trace context budget continued to pay off: L3's enumerated follow-ups plus L1's contrast let me design L4 as a principled tightening of L3's mechanism rather than a parameter sweep. The notes-with-NOTES.md context (70k chars / 17k tokens) cost is real but the directional signal it provides is much sharper than what brief-summary or metrics-only could give. The 10-day coverage gap was logged transparently rather than hidden -- a context-rich arm should still flag honesty issues per OBJECTIVE.md §8.
